messages.subject: Species metadata tag not found
parts:
Hi, 

I'm sure this is a really simple problem, and am not sure if its been addressed before :
I'm trying to generate a CSV table from my metadata tagged images, but I've used "Common name" as the parent tag for species. To confirm this, I used ExifTool separately to generate a csv and looked at the "Hierarchicalsubject' column to ensure that "Common name" appears as it should, and it does (see excel attached) 

RecordTable<- recordTable(inDir =testBrunei,
                          IDfrom = "metadata",
                          minDeltaTime = 1,
                          deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",
                          metadataSpeciesTag = "Common name",
                          timeZone = ("Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"),
                          writecsv = T,
                          outDir = testOut,
                          metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|")

I get the following error:

Warning: Belalong 18:   metadataSpeciesTag ' Common name' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'.
Warning: Belalong 18:   metadataSpeciesTag ' Common name' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'. Skipping

Incidentally, when I change the metadata species tag to a one-word parent tag ie. "Project", the table is generated as expected, however this isn't the species tag. Curious. 

Hope you can help :) really appreciate it!

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Species metadata tag not found
parts:
Hi,
please don't use spaces in the tag group names. While digiKam allows it, camtrapR has problems with it. This is because the tag group name ("Common name" in your case) is used as a column name, and R normally does not like spaces in column names. Therefore, to be on the safe side, camtrapR expects no spaces in the metadataSpeciesTag. 
I'll add a proper warning for that. 
It is also mentioned in vignette 2. The good news is that you can rename the tag group in digiKam and batch-update the metadata of all images. See vignette 2, under "What if non-hierarchical metadata tags were assigned to images already?", points 4 and 5. 
Cheers,
Jürgen
